name: canso
description: Spaceport Nova Scotia (Canso), Nova Scotia, Canada. Every value here is configuration; none is repeated in Python source.
coordinate_source: Cyclone-4M Abbreviated User's Guide section 2.2, pad 45.3 N 61.0 W. Spec II.1 records this as VERIFIED (SCIENCE Sec F.2).

coordinate_variants.source: alternate published coordinates recorded in spec II.1, SCIENCE Sec G.3
alternate published coordinates recorded in spec II.1, SCIENCE Sec G.3

corridor.source: Spec II.2 and II.10. The 2016 project description states all launch trajectories would be to the south over the Atlantic Ocean; the numeric fan is the engine default and is NOT a published three-sigma corridor.
assumptions: A_min_deg = 90 is set to due east, the azimuth that yields exactly the pad latitude, which is the minimum inclination a direct ascent can reach from 45.3 N. This is a consequence of the reachability algebra (spec II.2), not a range constraint read from the environmental assessment.

A_max_deg = 200 extends the fan past due south to 11.6 deg west of south, which is the azimuth of the advertised 98.1 deg SSO target, plus 8.4 deg of margin. The spec states this bound caps the maximum reachable inclination at about 104 deg.

NEITHER bound is a published figure. Spec II.2 and II.10 both mark them ASSUMPTION pending the environmental assessment Figure 2.9 three-sigma corridor check, which remains an open item (SCIENCE Sec G.2). See README 'Known-unread items'.
corridor.pending_verification: Environmental assessment Figure 2.9 three-sigma corridor check (SCIENCE Sec G.2)

car_source: Canadian Aviation Regulations 602.43 and 602.44, the launch authorization path recorded in spec II.8 and II.10. Referenced as static regulatory provenance; not parsed by the engine.

assumptions: No published operating-hours restriction for Canso was located. The pad is treated as continuously available so that operating hours never silently removes a window from a search. The engine reports this window on every response; changing it changes the answer with no code change.

conjunction.source: Spec II.8 names config key conjunction.miss_threshold_km and states the default is an ASSUMPTION value pending range feedback. 50 km is the engine default; no published Canso range feedback exists.

CUSTOM.source: Spec IV.1 type mapping: CUSTOM takes explicit h_t_km and i_t_deg from the request, so it carries no default inclination or altitude.

LEO.source: 45.1 deg is the advertised LEO class inclination from the project public material (spec II.10, SCIENCE Sec F.1, VERIFIED).
assumptions: h_t_km = 400 for the class default. The advertised inclination is published but the class altitude is not. 400 km is chosen because it is the altitude at which the spec's own plane-change penalty of 26.8 m/s (spec II.5, v_c = 7.67 km/s) reproduces; at 600 km the same formula gives 25.15 m/s. Nodal drift is always computed at whatever altitude the request carries, so this default affects only the penalty of an unreachable target.

POLAR.source: OneWeb-class polar inclination 87.9 deg from the project public material (spec II.10, SCIENCE Sec F.1, VERIFIED).

SSO.source: 98.1 deg is the SSO inclination at roughly 650 to 700 km (spec II.6); 674 km is the altitude the spec pairs with it in the drift table.
